eta.method: trend (log-linear fleet growth in the lead metro) with a mixture over denominator readings; Monte Carlo (N=200k) plus reference-class and proponent checks
eta.calc: Waymo rides/wk 250k (Apr 2025) -> 450k (Dec 2025) = 1.8x in 8 mo = 2.41x/yr; fleet ~2,500 in 6 cities (Dec 2025). Lead metro SF: Waymo ~1,000 (assumed ~40% of fleet, range 700-1,300; not in ledger). Denominator: broad (taxis + ride-hail on road at peak) ~6,000 (4k-12k; SFCTA background) weight 0.7 -> gap 6x; narrow (licensed taxis ~1,500) weight 0.3 -> gap 1.5x. Per-metro growth +55%/yr (30-100%; half of total log growth, fleet split over new metros). Broad: ln(6)/ln(1.55) = 4.1 yr after 2025.95 -> 2030.0 (+0.25-1.5 yr to a published count). MC: all p10 2027.7/p50 2030.0/p90 2033.5; broad 2028.9/2030.8/2034.2; narrow 2027.3/2028.0/2029.2. p90 widened to 2038 for a Cruise-type stall or strict L5 reading. Wuhan cross-check: Baidu 1,000+ vs ~10^4 taxis = >=10x -> later. Tesla's 2025 dates missed entirely (discounted). Prev v1 ETA '5-10 yrs (~2031-2036)'.
eta.cruxes: Earlier: a published per-city fleet count (CPUC/SFMTA/Waymo) with SF robotaxis >= licensed taxis, or Baidu/Pony fleet jumps in Wuhan/Shenzhen. Later: lead-metro fleet growth <30%/yr, a serious-incident shutdown, a ride-hail-inclusive denominator >10k, or a strict reading of '(L5)' (all deployments are geofenced L4).

eta.method: driver trend (exponential reliability growth, embodied doubling tied to METR horizons) plus a disclosure lag; Monte Carlo (N=200k); discounted-proponent and reference-class checks
eta.calc: Gap = interventions/shift I0 vs <=1. 84 s cycle -> 8*3600/84 = 343 cycles/shift; ~2% per-cycle failure (pi0.5 88-100% on trained tasks) x ~35% not self-recovered (STAR 78% lab recovery) = 2.4/shift, x2 for non-cycle failures -> I0 ~5 (1.5-30) = 2.3 doublings. Driver (robots-software, series metr-80-horizon-by-release --as-of 2026-10-06): p80 frontier 4.42 min (2024-09-12) -> 185.91 min (2026-04-07), 42x, 4.45-mo doubling (long run 6.4 mo); embodied doubling T_e assumed 11 mo (80% range 7-18) since VLA reliability lags software agents (REALM, VLA-survey events). Capability = 2025.9 + log2(5) x 11/12 = 2028.0; + disclosure lag median 1 yr (0.3-3). MC: capability p50 2027.9; ETA p10 2027.1/p50 2029.3/p90 2032.8; P(<=2031.76) = 0.83. p90 widened to 2034. label: Progressing: humanoids staff 1 station on day shifts; 24/7 robot-only line ~5 doublings, ETA ~2035
rationale: No event shows a multi-station line run only by general-purpose robots; the precursors are single-station humanoids on supervised 10-hour day shifts (Figure/BMW) and Digit's autonomous docking at GXO. A 10-robot line running 168 h with no humans needs about 30x the Blue Collar reliability (~4.9 doublings beyond it), plus robot-performed maintenance and a software changeover. Chaining that onto the Blue Collar capability (~2028) at an 11-month embodied doubling, plus ~1.5 yr of staging, gives ~2035 (80% range 2031-2046). The median is within 10 years and the drivers measurably move, so it is yellow; it sits near the 10-year line.

basis.rule: Milestone yellow (RUBRIC v2 §4): measurable progress on drivers the milestone is tied to (single-station full-shift humanoid deployments, autonomous docking, the autonomy trend), median ETA 2035 <= made_at + 10 yr; not green (median > 5 yr, no multi-station precursor)

eta.method: driver trend (exponential reliability growth chained from the Blue Collar capability) plus a staging lag; Monte Carlo (N=200k); reference-class check
eta.calc: ~10 robots (5 stations + movers + spares) x 168 h = 1,680 robot-h with no humans; 50% run success needs MTB-unrecoverable >= 1,680/ln2 = 2,424 robot-h; if peers/spares absorb 90% of interventions, Blue-Collar-sense MTBI >= 242 h vs 8 h = 30x = 4.9 doublings (97% absorbed: 3.2; 70%: 6.5). Driver (robots-software, series metr-80-horizon-by-release --as-of 2026-10-06): p80 frontier 4.42 min (2024-09-12) -> 185.91 min (2026-04-07), 42x, 4.45-mo doubling (long run 6.4 mo); embodied doubling T_e assumed 11 mo (80% range 7-18) since VLA reliability lags software agents (REALM, VLA-survey events). ETA = Blue Collar capability (2025.9 + log2(5) x 11/12 = 2028.0) + 4.9 x 11/12 (4.5 yr) + staging 1.5 yr (0.5-4) = 2034.0. MC: p10 2030.9/p50 2034.6/p90 2040.6; P(<=2036.76) = 0.71. p90 widened to 2046 (trend stall, or no one stages a humanoid-only line). Reference class: purpose-built robots took ~40 yr from Unimate (1961) to lights-out lines (~2001). Prev v1 ETA '>10 years (no evidenced path)'.
eta.cruxes: Earlier: a Blue Collar-grade disclosure (<=1 intervention/shift) by ~2028; >=10 humanoids on one line at one site; robot-performed battery swaps or maintenance in production; a staged multi-robot line demo (UBTech, Tesla, Figure). Later: intervention rates stuck >>1/shift, single-site fleets staying at <=5 units, humanoid programmes scaled back, or an embodied doubling time of >=15 months (pushes the median past 2036).

basis.path: Precursors: Figure 02 at BMW (one station, 10h shifts, support staff; Figure 03 successor); Digit at GXO (tote moves, ~4 h/battery, autonomous docking = self-charging precursor); UBTech Walker S2 500+ contracted for BYD/VW/Audi plants; Hyundai's planned Atlas deployment.
